title: Erlang Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: io:format writes output. ~n starts a new line. The module exports main so the command can call it.
notes: The module name lesson must match lesson.erl.

entries.name: Bind one value
entries.summary: Variables start with a capital letter. A variable can be bound only once in a function call.
notes: Matching a bound variable to a different value causes an error.

entries.name: Use a named label
entries.summary: Atoms are fixed labels. An unquoted atom usually starts with a lower-case letter.
notes: Names starting with capitals are variables, not atoms.

entries.name: Group a few values
entries.summary: A tuple can hold a status and a result. Pattern matching pulls its parts into names.
notes: The tuple shape and first atom must match.

entries.name: Split a list
entries.summary: [Head | Tail] separates the first item from the rest of a list.
notes: An empty list cannot match a head-and-tail pattern.

entries.name: Read a named key
entries.summary: A map keeps key-value pairs. maps:get reads the value for a key.

example.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Book = #{title => "Moon Trip", pages => 24},
    io:format("~s~n", [maps:get(title, Book)]).

notes: A missing key needs a fallback or an explicit check.

entries.name: Choose from patterns
entries.summary: case compares a value with patterns. The first matching branch supplies the result.

example.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Light = green,
    Message = case Light of red -> "Stop"; green -> "Go"; _ -> "Wait" end,
    io:format("~s~n", [Message]).

notes: Use semicolons between branches and end after the last branch.

entries.name: Check a number in a branch
entries.summary: A guard adds a small test after a pattern. when introduces that test.

example.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Score = 8,
    Message = case Score of N when N >= 5 -> "Pass"; _ -> "Try again" end,
    io:format("~s~n", [Message]).

notes: Not every function is allowed inside a guard.

entries.name: Call a local function
entries.summary: A named function can take an input and return its final expression.
notes: End each function definition with a period.

entries.name: Make a list by a rule
entries.summary: A list comprehension visits values and builds a result for each one.
notes: Use <- to take values from a list inside the comprehension.

entries.name: Send a message
entries.summary: A process has a mailbox. ! sends a message, and receive reads a matching message.

example.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    self() ! {score, 8},
    receive {score, N} -> io:format("~p~n", [N]) end.

notes: receive waits if no message matches; real waiting code often needs after.

entries.name: Start a small process
entries.summary: spawn starts a new process. It can send a result back to the parent process.

example.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Parent = self(),
    spawn(fun() -> Parent ! {answer, 4 * 2} end),
    receive {answer, N} -> io:format("~p~n", [N]) end.

notes: Processes have their own data; share results with messages.
